components.full_local_argument: Since Z_1^T Z_1≤I and range(Z_1) is contained in range(P), 0≤Z_1 Z_1^T≤P. Thus A(I−P)A^T≤A(I−Z_1 Z_1^T)A^T. Embedded by J_m, the right side equals padded A(I−padded P)padded A^T. For an orthogonal projector Q, AQ has squared singular values equal to the nonzero eigenvalues of AQA^T. Eigenvalue monotonicity therefore bounds every Schatten residual, including infinity. Padding preserves the optimal singular-value tail. Restrict/embed simulation applies to either direction and costs one product. Hence any successful padded output yields a square output with no larger residual and the same OPT.
components.input_conditions: k≤d≤min(m,n); a square hard instance A and a rank-k padded right projector.
components.parameter_and_cost_changes: Dimensions become m×n; same k, same product count, no increase in residual error.
components.preserved_model_properties: Padding preserves nonzero singular values and optimal tails. Arbitrary output outside the hard block cannot improve the extracted square residual.
components.transcript_control: Every padded query is simulated by one square product, restricting its input and embedding its output.
components.transformation: Let padded A=J_m A J_n^T. Write padded P=Zbar Zbar^T with orthonormal Zbar, set Z_1=J_n^T Zbar, complete range(Z_1) to a k-subspace of R^d and project onto it with P.

construction.definition: Choose integers 1≤k<d. Sample G in R^{d×k} with independent N(0,1/d) entries once and set A=GG^T. A is symmetric PSD and has rank k almost surely. For requested m×n dimensions with k<d≤min(m,n), embed as J_m A J_n^T using coordinate isometries.
construction.hidden_objects: G, A and range(G); the prior is independent of the algorithm seed.
construction.parameters: d,k public; the specified variance is 1/d. Relative-error consequence holds for all epsilon>0 and 1≤p≤infinity.
construction.public_information: Dimensions, rank-k PSD promise, Gaussian law and exact individual-matvec interface; the realized factor/range is not revealed.

escape_conditions.statement: After k independent Gaussian probes the responses span the hidden range almost surely.

escape_conditions.epistemic_note: Boundary of this exact-recovery argument; no quantitative additive-error lower bound supplied.
escape_conditions.statement: With a positive additive tolerance, success need not imply exact hidden-range equality.

hardness_claims.algorithm_coverage: All measurable randomized fully adaptive exact matvec algorithms with independent seed and cap q<k; no Krylov restriction.
hardness_claims.missing_lifting: No accuracy-dependent hardness or expected-budget lower bound asserted. Rectangular embedding uses the source-local Lemma 3.5 argument.
hardness_claims.regime_note: Zero distributional success below k for every 1≤k<d. k independent Gaussian probes recover the range almost surely. Use only as an O(k)-target branch in the full minimax lower bound.

oracle_realizations.choices_and_history: Algorithm chooses arbitrary measurable adaptive real vectors from past queries/replies and an independent seed. The instance is fixed before interaction.
oracle_realizations.cost: One individual product per vector; both directions cost two, b vectors cost b; computation and storage uncharged.
oracle_realizations.information_bottleneck: For q<k informative queries Lemma 4.1 leaves a (d−q)×(k−q) independent Gaussian block. After quotienting the exposed range its column space is nonatomic Haar, conditional on almost every actual transcript.
oracle_realizations.information_to_error: OPT_{p,k}(A)=0. Relative success requires A(I−P)=0, hence range(P)=range(G). The remaining nonatomic range cannot equal a fixed transcript-measurable output with positive conditional probability.
oracle_realizations.query_and_feedback: v in R^d returns Av=G(G^T v); transpose gives the same product. Padded Av restricts the input to the d-block and embeds the reply; padded transpose is simulated likewise.
oracle_realizations.sampling_and_reuse: One G and one A reused for all products; no fresh sample per query. Gaussian query probes in the upper witness are separate algorithm randomness.

use_restrictions: Rank baseline only; not the full accuracy-dependent construction.
The local padding argument must be checked independently; no Reviewer check claimed here.

links.note: Exact distributional lower bound and sharp k-probe witness; also proves PSD/rank membership.

research_use.reason: A zero optimal tail turns posterior range uncertainty into failure.

source_refs.locator: Lemma 3.5 pp.6–7; Lemma 4.2 p.9; Remark 4.3 p.10

summary: A=GG^T with d×k Gaussian G hides a nonatomic k-dimensional range; zero optimal tail forces exact range recovery.
title: Gaussian rank-k PSD exact-recovery family
use_when: Realize the k-query baseline for multiplicative LRA with zero tail.
